rationale: The pain is real and the Little Snitch pricing analogy ($45/license) gives a willingness-to-pay signal, but building a real-time process-level network and filesystem monitor on Linux requires kernel-level integration (eBPF, netlink sockets, inotify), a native GUI, and per-distro packaging — completely outside what this factory can produce with Claude prompts and a web page. Buyer clarity is moderate (security-conscious Linux developers) but the Linux desktop market is famously resistant to paying for software. Autonomy and buildability are both near zero for this category.
solution_plan: This is not a viable build for this factory. A functional Little Snitch equivalent for Linux requires native system programming, kernel interface expertise, and complex GUI work that cannot be delivered by a non-technical operator using Claude and a web form. Recommend dropping.
notes: Fails buildability_with_ai (score 2, floor is 6) and operational_autonomy (score 2, floor is 7). Total also below validate threshold. The analogy to Little Snitch pricing is encouraging as a market signal but the build path is entirely wrong for this factory.
